title: Help
intro: Answers to the usual questions, by area. Didn't find yours? Write to us at the bottom of the page.

photo.q: How do I add a receipt?
photo.a: Press Upload (the + on a phone) and take a photo or choose one: JPEG, PNG, HEIC or a PDF. Shop, date, every line and the total are read off it; check them and save.

long.q: A long receipt doesn't fit in one photo
long.a: Take it in several overlapping photos, up to 10 for one receipt. Lines caught in two photos are counted once.

email.q: How do I forward an e-receipt?
email.a: Profile shows your personal forwarding address. Forward the shop's e-mail receipt there from the address of your account, and it appears on Receipts a moment later — up to 20 a day.

manual.a: On Receipts or the upload screen choose “No receipt” and type in what, when and how much. It counts like any receipt, marked as having no document.

limit.q: How many receipts can I add?
limit.a: Reading a receipt costs a model call, so each account has a monthly limit of receipts read, shown on the upload screen and on Profile. Expenses typed in by hand don't count.

foreign.a: It is converted into your account's currency at the National Bank of Poland's rate, and both amounts are kept on the receipt.

how.a: Each line is put in a category as it is read. Lines the reader was unsure of wait on the Categories screen for a look.

fix.q: A line is in the wrong category
fix.a: Open the receipt and pick another category for the line. A name you correct for a shop is remembered for that shop's later receipts.

rules.q: Can I set my own rules?
rules.a: Yes: on Categories → Manage, create your own categories and rules — a keyword that always sends matching lines to a category.

kinds.a: Money goals — a spending ceiling or a sum to save — and lifestyle ones, such as eating out less, which are mapped to the categories they depend on.

advice.a: Once there are about 30 days of receipts. Advice is worked out from what you actually bought and says how much each step would change.

share.q: How do I share a budget with my family?
share.a: On Profile, create a household and send the invite link. Members see each other's receipts, read only, and the household's month and budget.

private.q: Can I keep a receipt to myself?
private.a: Yes: mark it private. It still counts in the household's total, but the others don't see what is on it.

kinds.a: A personal trip is your own money: it stays in the month, shown apart, with a budget of its own. A business trip is your employer's: it stays out of your budget and gets a per diem and a settlement.

perdiem.q: How is the per diem counted?
perdiem.a: Under the Polish business-travel regulation, from the departure and return times you enter: in Poland 45 zł a day, abroad the destination's rate; part days by hours, and meals provided reduce it.

settlement.q: How do I get the settlement for my employer?
settlement.a: On the business trip's page enter the advance you received and download the settlement as a PDF with every receipt's photo, or as CSV: expenses + per diem − advance.

export.q: How do I export my data?
export.a: Receipts and Statistics export the list or table on screen as CSV or JSON. Profile → “Download everything” gives one archive with all your data and the photos still kept. Export files are kept 7 days.

photos.q: Why did a receipt's photo disappear?
photos.a: Receipt photos are kept 90 days, then deleted; the lines and totals read from them stay. Download a business trip's settlement as PDF before then to keep its photos.

delete.q: How do I delete my account?
delete.a: Profile → Delete account, with your password. Everything goes for good; download your data first if you may need it.

confirm.q: I didn't get the confirmation email
confirm.a: Look in spam, then press “Send again” on the banner. Until the address is confirmed you can look around but not add receipts.

password.a: On the sign-in screen press “Forgot your password?” and follow the link sent to you within an hour.

install.q: Can I install it as an app?
install.a: Yes: Profile shows how to add it to the home screen of your phone or computer; it opens like an app.

contact.title: Didn't find an answer?
contact.intro: Write to us: the message goes to the people running Budget Agent, and you get a copy.
contact.sent: Thank you — your message is on its way, and a copy is in your inbox.
